prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1387; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a reported low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. Insured states the other vehicle crossed the centerline while making a turn. Both vehicles driven from scene. Insured reports mild neck discomfort but declined ambulance transport. Photos requested from insured.

Entry 2: Photos received from insured showing minor front bumper damage on insured vehicle and limited damage to the other vehicle's front bumper. Police report requested and pending. Other driver's insurer contacted to confirm liability position and policy details.

Entry 3: Claimant has retained counsel. Letter of representation received. All further communication to be directed through the attorney's office. Claimant's attorney requested medical authorization forms and the claimant's treatment records to date. Forms sent. Claimant reports neck strain diagnosed at urgent care with a recommendation for physical therapy.

Entry 4: Vehicle inspection completed by independent appraiser. Repair estimate received for insured vehicle and reviewed. Rental coverage confirmed under insured policy. Liability investigation ongoing; police report now received and notes the other driver's admission of a turning error. Attorney notified of preliminary liability findings.

Entry 5: Attorney submitted a demand package including urgent care records and physical therapy invoices. Claim reserve reviewed and adjusted for injury exposure. Medical records under review by claims nurse. File flagged for supervisor review before settlement discussions proceed.
